title: OpenClaw Desktop
role: Desktop application engineering, security hardening, product UX, test automation, and release engineering
summary: A Windows desktop client for working with a local OpenClaw gateway in WSL, professionalized around secure process boundaries, resilient connectivity, clear recovery states, and repeatable Windows delivery.
verifiedHighlights: Renderer-to-main IPC payloads and senders are validated at runtime.
Renderer-controlled shell text was replaced with closed command allowlists and positional arguments.
Diagnostics expose allow-listed summaries and recursively redact secrets and personal paths.
Settings and device credentials use Electron safeStorage when available, without a new plaintext fallback.
Gateway lifecycle, request correlation, reconnect backoff, settings storage, path conversion, IPC validation, and redaction have automated coverage.
Lint, type checking, automated tests, production build, and a Windows unpacked-package smoke test pass locally.
The dependency audit reports zero known vulnerabilities.
limitations: OpenClaw Desktop currently targets Windows 10/11 with WSL2 and systemd.
The gateway is intentionally restricted to local/private WebSocket endpoints; remote deployment and multi-user administration are out of scope.
Code signing and automatic release publication require maintainer-managed credentials and approval.
The showcase uses synthetic development data and is not a live service demonstration.

caseStudy.challenge: Turn an early desktop client into a portfolio-ready, maintainable application without exposing local OpenClaw data or disrupting the existing release history.
approach: Reconciled the newest accessible source against the public default branch by Git commit and tree identity.
Hardened IPC, WSL execution, navigation, external links, content security policy, filesystem boundaries, diagnostics, and secret storage.
Added explicit first-run, loading, empty, disconnected, and recovery states using the existing visual language.
Introduced deterministic tests, CI, and a Windows packaging smoke check.
Captured the actual renderer with a development-only fake-data adapter for a privacy-safe portfolio package.
outcomes: No raw OpenClaw configuration is returned by diagnostics.
No arbitrary command text crosses the renderer-to-main boundary.
The renderer runs sandboxed behind a restrictive content security policy and navigation controls.
Six required portfolio media assets document the product with synthetic information only.
caseStudy.verification: Local verification includes ESLint, TypeScript, 16 automated tests, a production build, dependency audit, secret scan, and Windows unpacked-package launch smoke check.
